We can use ls with path? The ls tool only lists current directory. There's no cd. But we can use find? No. We might need to use the filesystem functions to navigate? There's no cd. But maybe the current working directory is already the temp directory? We can try to list /tmp? But ls doesn't accept path. So we can't list /tmp. But maybe we can use find with path="/tmp"? find can search. But find returns items. But we want to list all files in /tmp. We can use find with path="/tmp" and name=None. That will list all items recursively. But we want all files and hidden. find will include hidden? It says it searches for files of any extension and directories within a specified path that match the given name. It doesn't mention hidden. But likely includes hidden. Let's try find.
